article.description: Vickie Johnson made two free throws with 14 seconds left as the Liberty rallied from a 15-point deficit in the second half for a thrilling 60-59 victory over the Detroit Shock.
article.headline: Liberty sneak past still-winless Shock
article.linkText: Weatherspoon records assist No. 1,000 in Liberty's win
article.story:
NEW YORK (AP) -- Teresa Weatherspoon found yet another teammate for a milestone assist, and the New York Liberty kept the Detroit Shock still searching for a victory. The 36-year old point guard became the first WNBA player to record 1,000 career assists in a 60-59 victory over the Shock on Wednesday night. Weatherspoon reached the mark with a pass to Crystal Robinson for a 3-pointer just 3:55 into the game. Robinson, who led the team in 3-point shooting percentage last season (.417), drilled the shot from the wing. The crowd of 13,181 fans stood, and Weatherspoon touched her hand to her heart and pointed to her teammates on the sideline. "Without these young ladies putting the ball in play for me, this wouldn't happen,'' she said. "So I thank them for this.'' Weatherspoon, who has started in every Liberty game in the WNBA's six-year history, finished with four assists, and two steals. She has 1,003 assists, 134 more than Sacramento's Ticha Penicheiro. Rookie Swin Cash had 15 points for the Shock (0-4), who have duplicated the start of their 1998 inaugural season. Vickie Johnson made two free throws with 14.9 seconds left as the Liberty erased a 15-point second-half deficit. Deanna Nolan tripped Johnson, who fell hard on her hip to the floor, to set up the winning free throws. She lay on the floor for a few minutes, and was helped off by the trainer. "VJ wanted to show us what a hero she is,'' forward Sue Wicks said. "That was big stuff.'' Dominique Canty then missed a shot in the paint to give New York (4-1) the win. Tari Phillips added 16 points, and Robinson had 10 for the Liberty, who shot just 20 percent in the first half. Wendy Palmer had 10 points and eight rebounds for Detroit, and Astou Ndiaye-Diatta added nine points. Phillips stole the ball and fed Johnson for a layup for the Liberty's first lead of the second half, 56-55, with 2:41 left. Ndiaye-Diatta scored on a bank shot, but Johnson answered with a jumper. Ndiaye-Diatta's jumper gave Detroit a 59-58 lead with 1:36 left. Cash, the No. 2 pick in this year's draft from NCAA champion Connecticut, finished 6-for-12 from the field and had eight rebounds. "They say there's a lot of magic in this building, and it must be true'' said Cash, the Final Four MVP. "We were up 15 and really thought we had it in the bag. When you get in situations like that, you need chemistry to win games.'' Canty played her first game of the season after breaking her left hand in the first week of training camp. She played 10 minutes in a reserve role and finished with two points. "We've been losing games in the last 18 minutes,'' Detroit coach Greg Williams said. "We lost today in the last 14 seconds. That's progress for this young team.'' The Liberty, who trailed 45-30 with 12:40 left, missed 13 of their first 16 shots.

Game notes
Rosie O'Donnell and rock musician Joan Jett were in attendance. ... The Shock shot 49 percent from the field. ... The Liberty had five players averaging in double-figure scoring entering the game. ... Weatherspoon, a two-time defensive player of the year, is also the league's career leader with 393 steals. ... New York has won four straight after dropping the season-opener to the defending champion Los Angeles Sparks.
